name: Practitioner and trade-press sources naming a writing form
licence: cite-only, read in a browser and cited
totalDerivedFrom: no fixed list: newsroom and newsletter craft writing, the trade press and essays by people who write the form, read where criticism had named nothing, from 2026-09-09

terms.note: form: the essay run as a numbered sequence of capped posts, named in the trade press and in criticism, with craft advice on how to write it and a body of work by named journalists from 2016. Proposal B14 #1, minted with no manifestation on instruction. Written and attested 2026-09-09.
read as the strongest candidate for a Newsletters leaf; the piece describes one newspaper's product and its workflow, names no generic form and no other newsroom writing in it
a named register with a documented origin in sports talk radio, but it belongs to opinion writing at speed and appears in columns as much as in posts; it needs a parent this pass did not have
defined by its effect on a discussion rather than by how the writing is made, so it names a behaviour and not a manner
a practice of reproduction rather than of authorship
the article is mostly about software conversation threading; its passage on numbered essays posted in real time is cited on the Tweetstorm cell

a genuinely named blog form, posts whose titles link out with a note attached, and the filter-style weblog this collection could not name in B10; not minted because Blogs already has a leaf and was not one of the two gaps
a named form with a described structure and an enormous body of work; it belongs under Blogs rather than under either gap
a real newsroom register, news you can use, and the one most newsletters are written in; it sits across journalism rather than under Newsletters, so it needs a parent this pass did not have
the mailing-list article defines digest as a delivery mode, all of a day's messages combined into one email, which is a schedule and not a manner
